claim.quote: We report a new high-precision measurement of kaonic hydrogen X-ray transitions performed by the SIDDHARTA-2 experiment

date.locator: arXiv abstract page, submission date (arXiv:2607.13952 v1)

key_value_text.value: Kaonic hydrogen 1s shift ε = −303.0 ± 17.0 (stat.) ± 2.5 (syst.) eV and width Γ = 607 ± 62 (stat.) ± 6 (syst.) eV, from 237 pb⁻¹

name: High-precision measurement of the kaonic hydrogen 1s level shift and width with SIDDHARTA-2

summary.plain: SIDDHARTA-2 re-measured the X-rays from kaonic hydrogen and reports values of the strong-force shift and width of the atom's ground state that it calls the most precise to date, about twice as precise as the previous SIDDHARTA result.
summary.technical: SIDDHARTA-2 at DAΦNE: kaonic hydrogen X-ray transitions from 237 pb⁻¹ taken from December 2023 to February 2024 and April to May 2024; 1s shift ε = −303.0 ± 17.0 (stat.) ± 2.5 (syst.) eV and width Γ = 607 ± 62 (stat.) ± 6 (syst.) eV, improving the precision by about a factor of two over SIDDHARTA.

title: High-precision measurement of the kaonic hydrogen 1s level shift and width with SIDDHARTA-2
why_it_matters: The abstract says the values are the most precise determination to date and tighten the experimental constraints on the low-energy antikaon-nucleon interaction and the Λ(1405) description.
